1. Corporate girl- working in sports has been my dream since I was 17 & after walking away from my career from 23-28 to take care of my mom, I’m finally back in a sports role & SO proud of the steps I’ve taken in the corporate space this year.
2. Decorating a home makes me come alive. Home is my most creative space. I love colors and patterns and textures and making my space reflect me brings me JOY.
3. Travel keeps me sane. I have had to learn how short life is & because of that im working and saving to be able to LIVE. I have a never ending bucket list & also love sharing about the beautiful places I’ve already been. 
4. Budgeting has never had to be forefront of my mind due to circumstances I wouldn’t wish on anyone, but now that I’m chasing my corporate dreams (which don’t pay a lot) I want to be smart with money for the first time in my life. It’s hard & I’m not perfect (I will always be a gift giver no matter the struggle) but I’m attempting to learn and share along the way.
5. My mental health tanked when I lost my mom and grandma both to cancer 3 weeks apart. I thought I could outsmart grief by suppressing but im paying the price years later. As someone with low self-worth anyway I’m navigating feelings of loneliness and grief using all the tools I can possibly gather. You are NOT alone.

(Nuanced notes below 👇 ) This is the framework I use to determine which accounts I prioritize first. How do you prioritize your accounts?

The nuanced version:
1. Emergency fund. Keep it in a HYSA or if it’s large (above £10k) consider a cash ISA.

2.Employer match pension. Take advantage of the bonus you get from your employer. Opting out is giving yourself a pay cut for no reason.

3. Individual Savings Accounts. This could be S&S ISA or LISA, or both. How you want to prioritize depends on your goals and the property you are looking for.

4. SIPP. You do get the tax savings here. Ideally if your employer offers a salary sacrifice, I would do that instead to save on National Insurance and student loan contributions.

5. General account. If you’ve maxed out everything above, it’s time to just use a general account. There’s no tax benefits here so just keep that in mind.

no bake biscoff cheesecake 🍰🤎
ingredients:
2 packs of biscoff cookies 
12 tbsp salted butter melted 
1.5 tbsp light brown sugar 

24 oz cream cheese (room temperature)
1/2 cup powdered sugar 
1/2 cup biscoff spread 
1 tbsp vanilla extract 

1 1/2 cups heavy whipping cream 
1/2 cup powdered sugar 

1/3 cup biscoff spread melted 
6 biscoff cookies crushed
2 biscoff cookies for topping

instructions 🍰 
place 2 packs of biscoff cookies into a blender or food processor and blend until they form fine crumbs.
in a springform pan, combine the cookie crumbs with 1.5 tbsp of brown sugar, and 12 tbsp of melted butter.
mix until the texture resembles wet sand and the crumbs clump when pressed.
press the mixture firmly into the bottom of the pan, slightly pressing some crumbs up the side to create the crust.
place in the refrigerator for 30 minutes so the crust can firm up.

in a large bowl beat 24 oz of room temperature cream cheese until smooth.
add in 1/2 cup of biscoff spread, 1 tbsp vanilla extract, and 1/2 cup of powdered sugar.
mix together until silky.

in a separate bowl, whip together 1/2 cups of heavy cream and 1/2 cup of powdered sugar.
gently fold in the whipped cream into the cream cheese filling. do not over mix 
spread the cheesecake filling evenly over the chilled crust and smooth the top. refrigerate overnight until fully set.

melt 1/3 cup of the biscoff spread.
pour it over the cold cheesecake and gently spread it to the edges. place back in the fridge for 30 minutes to set the biscoff topping.

crush about 6 biscoff cookies and place it around the edges of the cheesecake.
add 2 full biscoff cookies to the top of your cheesecake.
slice and serve chilled

spicy vodka chicken parmesan sandwich 🌶️ 🍝 🥖 
ingredients
for the chicken:
2 thinly sliced chicken breast 
all purpose flour 
seasonings:onion powder, garlic powder, basil, oregano, salt, black pepper, and paprika
2 eggs whisked 
seasoned panko bread crumbs 
grated parmesan
oil for frying 
vodka sauce 
fresh mozzarella 

vodka sauce:
1/4 onion diced
1/2 tbsp minced garlic 
tomato paste 
red pepper flakes
vodka
heavy cream 
seasonings: salt, black pepper, garlic powder, parsley, oregano, basil
handful of freshly grated parmesan cheese 

sandwhich:
sub rolls
pesto sauce
vodka sauce
chicken parm
grated parmesan cheese
top with melted butter and parsley

Instructions
Pat dry your 2 thinly sliced chicken breasts.
Season both sides with onion powder, garlic powder, basil, oregano, salt, black pepper, and paprika.
Set up breading station:
Bowl 1: all-purpose flour with seasonings
Bowl 2: whisked eggs
Bowl 3: seasoned panko + grated parmesan

Bread the chicken:
Dredge in flour → dip in egg → coat in panko mixture (press firmly).

Heat oil over medium-high heat.
Fry chicken 3–4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through.
Remove and drain on a rack or paper towels.

Spoon vodka sauce over each piece and top with fresh mozzarella.
Broil or cover briefly until melted.

Spicy Vodka Sauce
In a pan over medium heat:
Sauté diced onion in oil until softened (2–3 minutes).
Add minced garlic and cook until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste and cook 2–3 minutes until slightly darkened.
Add red pepper flakes.
Pour in vodka and let it simmer 1–2 minutes to cook off.
Lower heat and stir in heavy cream.
Season with salt, black pepper, garlic powder, parsley, oregano, and basil.
Simmer until smooth and slightly thickened.
Stir in freshly grated parmesan until creamy.

Prep bread
Lightly toast sub rolls in the oven.
Spread pesto on the top bun.
Spoon vodka sauce on the bottom bun.
Add crispy chicken parm and top with extra spicy vodka sauce.
Sprinkle grated parmesan.
Brush top with melted butter and parsley.

Air fry at 400F for 12 minutes.

Chop the shrimp into small pieces and add in to a bowl.

Spread the rice evenly into a greased baking dish.

Bake at 400F for 15 min. Then broil for 2-3 minutes on high.

You don’t need more money to start, you need a system that pays you first automatically and consistently. Folks love to debate good debt versus bad debt, but for most of you, there’s no such thing as good debt. Debt used for leverage only works when you already have discipline, margin, and a clear plan, and most aren’t there yet. Car loans, credit cards, and financing things you can’t afford will quietly block your progress for years. It’s almost impossible to build wealth while interest is working against you. Get your debts in order first, then talk about leverage. #financialfreedom #moneytok #moneytips #wealthymindset #millionairemindset

Debt owns you when your future income is already committed to someone else. If every raise, bonus, or paycheck is pre-spent on monthly obligations, you’re not lacking income, you’re lacking margin. people think getting in shape means going from 0 → 100 overnight. Two hour workouts. Training every day. Completely changing your diet. And then when it becomes overwhelming… they quit.

Real progress usually looks much simpler.

It’s going for a walk when you didn’t feel like it.
It’s doing a 20 to 30 minute workout instead of skipping it.
It’s choosing consistency even when the workout isn’t perfect.

Fitness isn’t about being intense for a week.
It’s about showing up in small ways over and over again.

Those small habits compound into real results.

So if you’re starting your fitness journey, don’t focus on doing everything. Focus on doing something consistently.

Consistency will always beat intensity you can’t maintain.

‼️ How to Study After School When All You Wanna Do Is Sleep for 10 Years 😴📚 

😮‍💨 3:00 – 3:30 PM → Decompress time
Reach home, change clothes, drink water. No studying, no guilt. Let your brain breathe after school.

🍽️ 3:30 – 4:00 PM → Snack and chill
Eat something light and relax a bit. This prevents the post school crash later.

📚 4:00 – 5:15 PM → Study Block 1
Start with easy tasks. Revise what was taught today or do light subjects to warm up your brain.

🚶‍♀️ 5:15 – 5:30 PM → Break
Walk around, stretch, fresh air. No bed, no scrolling.

📘 5:30 – 6:45 PM → Study Block 2
Do your main subject or one heavy chapter. Use active studying like questions and explanations.

🍛 6:45 – 7:30 PM → Dinner and rest
Eat calmly. Avoid heavy food so you don’t feel sleepy.

🚿 7:30 – 7:50 PM → Reset routine
Quick shower or face wash. This is your second energy boost of the day.

📖 7:50 – 9:15 PM → Study Block 3
This is your most productive slot. Focus on practice questions, numericals, or weak topics.

💧 9:15 – 9:30 PM → Short break
Water, stretching, slow music. Keep it low effort.

📓 9:30 – 10:15 PM → Light revision
Flashcards, summaries, or quick review. No heavy learning here.

😌 10:15 – 10:30 PM → Wind down
Pack your bag, tidy your desk, prepare for tomorrow.

🛌 10:30 PM onwards → Sleep
Proper sleep is non negotiable if you want energy tomorrow.

How to study like Japanese students‼️

📓 Kaizen mindset
Japanese students focus on small daily improvement. Even thirty minutes every day beats random long study days. Consistency over intensity always wins.

🧠 Shūkanika meaning habit building
They rely on routine, not motivation. Same study time, same place, same flow. Your brain learns to focus automatically.

✏️ Kaki nagara manabu meaning learn by writing
Instead of just reading, they write summaries, formulas, and explanations again and again. Writing locks information into memory.

📖 Fukushū meaning revision
Revision is non negotiable. They revise the same topic multiple times in short sessions instead of cramming once.

⏳ Shōjikan shūchū meaning short focused study
They study in short, distraction free blocks. Deep focus for a short time beats distracted long hours.

🧹 Seiri seiton meaning organised space

‼️How to study and actually remember

🔄 Instead of finishing one chapter in one go, switch between two similar topics. It feels harder, but your brain remembers better when it learns to tell things apart.

⏱️ Don’t revise immediately. Come back to the topic after a few hours. That small gap makes the memory stick longer.

🗺️ Try studying the same subject in the same spot every day. Over time, just sitting there will put your brain into study mode.

🎧 Record yourself explaining the topic like you’re teaching a friend. Listen to it later while walking or resting. It feels weird, but it works.

🧩 Attempt questions before you feel “ready.” Getting things wrong first actually helps your brain understand faster.

🧠 Force yourself to shrink the topic into a few main ideas. If you can’t explain it simply, you probably haven’t understood it yet.

🛌 Read a short summary before sleeping, then test yourself the next morning. Sleep does half the remembering for you.

‼️ How to predict exam questions (smart study strategies)

📚 Look at past exam papers
Teachers often repeat question styles and topics. Go through past papers and notice which chapters or question patterns appear frequently.

🧠 Pay attention to what teachers emphasize
If a teacher repeats a concept, writes it on the board, or spends extra time explaining it, there’s a high chance it could appear in the exam.

✏️ Focus on key topics in each chapter
Not every detail becomes a question. Definitions, formulas, diagrams, and main concepts are much more likely to be tested.

📖 Check review questions in textbooks
End-of-chapter questions and practice exercises are often very similar to real exam questions.

🔁 Notice patterns in assignments and tests
Homework, quizzes, and class tests often give clues about the type of questions teachers prefer.

The Goblet Squat is one of the foundational movements when it comes to kettlebell training.

Learning proper technique doesn’t begin when you start squatting. It starts with the setup. 

I like having the kettlebell handle in line with the midline of my foot (where my shoelaces start). There could be variation of this if you like it closer to your heel. 

From here, my glutes are above my knees, butt is still down and my chest is up. I break the kettlebell in half like I’m trying to split a piece of wood to engage my lats.

I pull the kettlebell into the front rack position, elbows down and arms are vertical not out. Drop your hips down and go all the way down until your thighs are parallel. Then use your feet to drive back up. 

You don’t want your spine rounded or your torso leaning forward, try and stay upright. Bracing your core and stacking your ribs should help with this.

Miso marinated cod, jasmine rice, and smashed cucumber Asian Salad 🐟

Cud Cooks x @alaskaseafooduk AD

Here is a delicious summer recipe; miso marinated cod served with jasmine rice and everyone's favourite Asian cucumber salad. It's healthy, full of protein, and comes together really quickly - the perfect summer dinner party dish. 

I've made this with the Miso Marinated Black Cod from @alaskaseafooduk. It's wild caught in Alaska, full of goodness, and comes pre-marinated in a delicious authentic Japanese miso sauce. Super easy to cook and takes a lot of the effort out. Full recipe below!

1. Smash 2 cucumbers with something heavy like a rolling pin. Chop these diagonally and place in a bowl with a generous pinch of fine salt. Mix and set aside for a minimum of 10 minutes to draw out the excess moisture
2. Start the cooking of your jasmine rice according to packet instructions
3. Put some oil in an oven-proof frying pan or skillet on a medium heat. Once hot, caramelise the Miso Marinated Black Cod from @alaskaseafooduk flesh side down for 1-2 minutes. Turn, and transfer the pan to a preheated 200C oven for c. 15 minutes
3. Whilst the fish is cooking, finish the salad. Drain the excess moisture from the cucumber, and finely slice 2 spring onions, 2 red chillies, and a small bunch of coriander stalks
4. In a bowl, add the cucumber, spring onions, red chillies, coriander, 4 finely diced garlic cloves, 2 tsp sugar, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tbsp sesame oil, 2 tbsp crispy chilli oil, and toasted sesame seeds. Mix well. Right before serving, add coriander leaves
5. Remove the fish from the oven, and plate on top of the rice. Serve the salad on the side. Serve with a wedge of lime.

CHARRED HISPI CABBAGE WITH MISO BUTTER AND SMOKED SALT 🥬🔥 RECIPE ⬇️

@cud_cooks x @maldonsalt AD

Smoky, savoury, and rich with umami - this simple side dish turns humble cabbage into something genuinely special. Charred hispi cabbage is basted in golden miso butter, finished with fresh lime, and brought to life with Maldon’s Smoked Sea Salt. A flavour bomb of smoke, tang, and depth. This is a perfect side dish, or a veggie alternative for a roast.

Slice 1 whole hispi cabbage in half lengthways. Heat some olive oil in a pan. Fry cut-side down over high heat for 4-5 mins until deeply browned and charred. Transfer to a 200°C oven and roast for 25-30 mins until tender.

Meanwhile, make the miso butter: mix 80g softened unsalted butter with 1 tbsp miso paste, the juice and zest of ½ lime, and a generous pinch of Maldon Smoked Sea Salt.

Return the cooked cabbage to the pan, add a large spoonful of miso butter, and baste until glossy and caramelised. Finish with extra miso butter, lime juice, lime zest, and another pinch of Maldon Smoked Sea Salt.

Beef Wellington & Red Wine Jus 🥩🍷

Here’s a favourite centerpiece: Beef Wellington! Perfect for Christmas, this version features a 1kg beef fillet, a rich chestnut and mushroom duxelles with a hint of truffle oil, and golden puff pastry topped with a thyme-studded lattice. It’s paired with a rich, silky red wine jus for an unforgettable main dish. This recipe is part of my partnership with @robertwelchuk, featuring their Professional Knives, Campden Low Casserole Pot, and Campden Saucepan range – ideal for perfecting each step. Full recipe below.

Prepare the beef: Sear a 1kg center-cut beef fillet in the Campden Low Casserole Pot until golden on all sides (1-2 min per side). Cool, then brush with mustard.

Make the duxelles: In the same pot, cook 2 diced shallots in 30g butter and 2 tbsp truffle oil until softened. Add 500g finely chopped mushrooms, 100g finely chopped chestnuts, finely chopped thyme, rosemary and garlic. Cook until all moisture evaporates and cool.

Spinach crepes: Blanch 100g spinach and refresh in ice water. Blend spinach with 150g milk, then whisk into 2 eggs and 100g plain flour. Cook 4 thin crepes in a non-stick pan and cool.

Assemble: On cling film, lay the crepes flat, overlap with 8 slices of prosciutto, and spread duxelles to 0.5cm layer. Roll tightly around the beef using cling film, chill to set. Wrap the beef in puff pastry, add a lattice top (using a lattice cutter), and brush with egg wash. Garnish the gaps in the lattice with sprigs of thyme

Bake: Bake at 200°C for 30 minutes. Rest for 15 minutes.

Red wine jus: Roast 1kg beef bones, 2 marrow bones, 500g beef offcuts, and 4 shallots at 220°C until browned - around 30 mins. Add to a Campden Saucepan and add 500ml red wine, and bring to boil. Then add 1l water, thyme, rosemary, bay leaves, and peppercorns. Simmer for 3-4 hours, strain, and reduce to a silky jus that coats a spoon. Season to taste.

Slice the Wellington (1.5 inches), serve with jus, and enjoy this show-stopping dish!

SLOW-BRAISED CHICKEN // CELERIAC MASH // TARRAGON CAPER SAUCE 🍋🍗 RECIPE ⬇️

Golden, crisp-skinned chicken legs slow-braised until tender, served over silky celeriac mash and finished with a bright tarragon, lemon and caper sauce.

Recipe (serves 3)

Peel and dice 2 whole celeriac into small 3-5mm squares. Melt 50g unsalted butter in a wide pan, add the celeriac with a generous pinch of salt, and cook over a medium heat for around 45 minutes, stirring frequently, until completely soft and most of the moisture has evaporated.
Stir through 150ml double cream and 100ml chicken stock, then blend until completely smooth. Check seasoning and keep warm.
Season 3 whole chicken legs  generously with salt and pepper. Heat 2 tbsp La Española Cooking Olive Oil in an ovenproof pan and sear the chicken skin-side down until deeply golden and crisp. Remove from the pan.
Lower the heat and soften 4 finely chopped garlic cloves. Add 4-5 thyme sprigs, then deglaze with 500ml chicken stock. Return the chicken to the pan, cover with a lid and cook in a 160°C oven for 45 minutes.
Remove the chicken and thyme stalks, then reduce the stock by roughly two-thirds. Stir through 2 tbsp crème fraîche and 1 tsp Dijon mustard, reducing again until the sauce coats the back of a spoon (add a splash more stock if needed).
Finish with the zest of ½ lemon, a squeeze of lemon juice, 3 tbsp chopped capers, and a handful of finely chopped fresh tarragon.
Spoon the celeriac mash onto plates, top with the chicken and sauce, and finish with a generous drizzle of La Española Extra Virgin Olive Oil.

MARRY ME MASH 🥔✨ Recipe below ⬇️

This is the ultimate recipe for luxurious mashed potato. Ultra-smooth, buttery, garlic-thyme infused, finished with white pepper and nutmeg. Make no mistake - this is pure indulgence, and it will make your guests so silent at the table.

Marry Me Mash:

Peel and cube 1kg Maris Piper potatoes. Add to cold salted water, bring to the boil, then simmer gently until completely tender. Drain and leave to steam dry for 20-30 minutes (this step is key for texture).
Meanwhile, gently simmer 200ml whole milk and 200ml double cream with 4 chopped garlic cloves and 3-4 thyme sprigs for 30 minutes to infuse. Strain and keep warm.
Pass the dried potatoes through a ricer, then fold through 150g melted butter. For extra smoothness, push through a fine mesh sieve.
Add the warm infused cream one ladle at a time until silky and smooth but still holding its shape. Season with fine salt, white pepper and a small grating of nutmeg. Taste and adjust.
Bonus recipe - Braised Short Rib (perfect with this mash):

Season 3-4 large beef short ribs generously with salt and pepper and sear in a hot casserole pot with 1 tbsp oil until deeply browned. Remove.
In the same pot soften 1 diced onion, 2 diced celery sticks and 2 diced carrots. Add 2 tbsp tomato purée, 3 sliced garlic cloves, 3 thyme sprigs and 2 bay leaves. Deglaze with 500ml red wine, reduce slightly, then add enough beef stock (around 750ml-1L) to fully submerge the ribs.
Return the ribs, cover and cook at 130°C for 4 hours until spoon tender. Remove the ribs, strain and remove the fat from the sauce (use a separator jug if you have one). Pass through a fine sieve and then reduce it until glossy and thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. Return the ribs to the sauce and baste.
Silky mash. Sticky, rich beef. Absolute comfort food - elevated.

PERFECT PORK BELLY 🐖🔥 RECIPE ⬇️

Crispy skin, tender meat, caramelised fennel, and a rich cider gravy - this is the perfect pork belly. Slow-roasted for tenderness, finished at high heat for crackling, and served with roasted fennel, shallots, apples, and thyme.

Recipe below ⬇️

Pork: Place a 2.5kg pork belly in the fridge uncovered overnight. Next day, wrap foil so it covers just the meat, leaving skin exposed. Brush with olive oil, season with salt, and roast at 140°C for 2½ hours.
Veg: In a casserole pot, combine 2 quartered fennel bulbs, 6 halved shallots, 1 halved garlic bulb, 2 apples (cut into sixths), thyme, fennel seeds, salt, pepper, and olive oil. Roast for 1 hour in the same oven.
Combine: Pour pork juices into the veg, then roast both together at 240°C for 30-40 mins to crisp the skin. Remove the pork and rest uncovered
Gravy: Deglaze the casserole with 1-2 bottles cider, boil, strain, and reduce until glossy.
Serve the veg in a dish, spoon over the cider gravy, and slice the pork to serve on top.

PERFECT ROAST CHICKEN WITH GARLIC & TARRAGON MAYONNAISE 🍗✨ RECIPE ⬇️

Crisp, golden skin, juicy meat, rich gravy, and the most addictive homemade garlic and tarragon mayonnaise - this is the ultimate roast chicken. Simple, classic, and made even better with Maldon Garlic Sea Salt.

Recipe:
Take 1 whole quality chicken. Stuff the cavity with 2 shallots, 2 garlic cloves, a few sprigs of thyme, and a generous pinch of Maldon Sea Salt. Pat the skin dry, brush all over with olive oil, and season generously with Maldon Garlic Sea Salt.

In an oven-safe pan, add 4 peeled shallots, 4 garlic cloves, sprigs of thyme and rosemary, and a drizzle of olive oil. Place a wire rack over the top and set the chicken on it - this lets the bird crisp all over while the juices drip into the pan. Roast at 180°C for around 1 hour 15 minutes, or until golden and cooked through.

Garlic & Tarragon Mayonnaise:
In a food processor, combine 2 egg yolks, 1 tbsp Dijon mustard, juice of ½ lemon, 2 tbsp chardonnay vinegar, a pinch of caster sugar, a pinch of Maldon Garlic Sea Salt, and 1 grated garlic clove. Blend briefly. With the motor running, slowly drizzle in 150g vegetable oil and 100g virgin rapeseed oil until thick and glossy. Fold through a handful of finely chopped fresh tarragon.

Gravy:
Once the chicken is cooked, rest it in a warm place. Pour 500ml cider into the roasting pan to deglaze, scraping up all the caramelised bits. Add 500ml chicken stock and bring to a boil. Sieve into a saucepan, add 2-3 knobs of butter, and reduce until it coats the back of a spoon.

Carve the chicken, serve with the gravy and a generous spoonful of the garlic and tarragon mayonnaise. Heaven.

A BRITISH CLASSIC - FISH & CHIPS 🇬🇧🐟🍟

@ed.cudlipp x @Waitrose & Partners AD

There are few things better than proper fish and chips. For this one I went all in and made everything from scratch using ingredients from Waitrose - crispy, golden cod, double-fried chips, homemade tartare sauce, all finished with Waitrose Chip Shop Curry Sauce. The cod came fresh from the Waitrose fish counter (all Waitrose fish is responsibly sourced).

Recipe (serves 2):

- Peel 5–6 Maris Piper potatoes, cut into chunky chips and rinse until water runs clear. Add to salted cold water, bring to the boil and cook ~7 mins until just tender.
- Drain, steam dry, then fry at 135°C for ~6 mins. Remove and cool completely.
- Tartare sauce: make mayo by blending 2 egg yolks, 1 tsp Dijon mustard, ½ lemon juice, 2 tbsp chardonnay vinegar, pinch sugar and salt, then slowly add 150g veg oil and 100g rapeseed oil. Mix 6 tbsp with chopped cornichons, capers, lemon juice, parsley and tarragon. Chill.
- Batter: whisk 200g flour, 100g cornflour, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp baking powder and salt. Add 400ml cold sparkling water to form a loose batter.
- Lightly flour and batter two cod fillets from the Waitrose fish counter.
- Fry chips again at 185°C for ~5 mins until golden and crisp. Season well.
- Fry fish at 180°C for 5–8 mins until crisp and golden. Season.
- Warm Waitrose Chip Shop Curry Sauce and serve with fish, chips and tartare.

Golden fish. Proper chips. Curry sauce on the side. Exactly how it should be.

HOT HONEY WINGS 🔥🍯 RECIPE ⬇️

Crispy, sticky, spicy, and sweet - these Hot Honey Wings are dangerously addictive. Glazed in melted butter, honey, and hot sauce, and finished with Maldon’s Chilli Sea Salt for a fiery, flaky kick. Perfect for game day, dinner, or just a Friday night craving.

Recipe:
For 20 winglets (whole chicken wings, cut in half) (serves 2), toss the wings in 1 tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp garlic powder, 1 tbsp onion powder, 1 tbsp smoked paprika, and a generous pinch of Maldon Chilli Sea Salt. Arrange on a wire rack over a tray and bake at 170°C for 1 hour, until golden and crisp.

For the hot honey glaze, melt 50g butter with 4 tbsp honey, 4 tbsp Frank’s Hot Sauce, 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar, and a pinch of Maldon Chilli Sea Salt. Stir to combine over low heat.

Once the wings are cooked, toss them generously in the sauce until coated and sticky. Finish with fresh lemon juice, chopped chives, and an extra sprinkle of Maldon Chilli Sea Salt.

Yes… you have to invest the money within a Roth IRA🤨

I realize that your average person may not know this but there is no excuse for “financial gurus” to be surprised by this.❌

A Roth IRA is an investment vehicle. Just like a car 🚗 , it won’t drive itself. Well I guess cars can drive themselves now, but anyways.

You must “drive” the investment vehicle. Meaning, you must choose the investments. Typically, something known as the “Money Market” is the default fund that your money gets put in. Essentially this is cash.💵 It’ll earn a small interest rate but not much.

If you never choose your investments your money will never begin working for you. Don’t make that mistake! Make sure your money is invested!

     🐔CIULAMA DE PUI CU CIUPERCI 

   INGREDIENTE: 
- pulpe de pui 800 gr (fie dezosate sau de care aveți) 
- 500 gr ciuperci 
- o ceapă
- 2,3 căței usturoi
- sare, piper 
- supă de pui 500 ml
- 220-250 gr smântână cu 25% grasime 
- 3 linguri făină 
  
 Mod de prepare: 
   Carnea de pui o condimentați cu sare, piper și boia dulce și o puneți la prăjit pe o parte și cealaltă foarte bine. 
   După ce s-a prăjit carnea  puneți la călit o ceapă tocată mărunt 2,3 minute, iar apoi cateii de usturoi tocați. Mai lăsați 2,3 minute la călit și apoi adăugați ciupercile tăiate fâșii subțiri. 
    Mestecați ciupercile și le lăsați la foc mic să scadă. Ele vor lăsa apa din ele în tigaie. Într-un bol puneți smântâna, făina și le mestecați puțin. 
  Treptat adăugați supa de pui călduță și mestecați continuu până se omogenizează totul bine. 
 Puneți conținutul în tigaie când au scăzut ciupercile de tot și nu mai au apă. 
  Mestecați puțin și adăugați și carnea. Apoi mestecați continuu până se îngroașă făina pt a nu se prinde de tigaie. Mai lăsați la foc câteva minute, condimentați cu sare și piper și la final pătrunjel.

Ingredients:
Olive oil
1 tbsp butter
1/2 small onion
2 chicken breasts
1 cup Parmesan cheese
1/4 cup mozzarella cheese
2 cups chicken broth
1/2 cup milk (or heavy cream)
3 tbsp cream cheese
1 pound pasta noodles
Seasonings: garlic powder, onion powder, Tony’s creole, paprika, pepper

How to:
•in a pan on medium heat add olive oil
•next add your seasoned chicken breasts. cook & then remove from the pan
•add in butter & onion and cook for 1-2 mins then add chicken broth
•season the sauce with garlic, onion & tonys then mix & add milk(or cream)
•add the parm & mozzarella cheese and mix until combined 
•add the cream cheese, mix until melted & combined. Then add your cooked pasta noodles
•top with a bit more cheese, add the chicken back in and let simmer on low for couple mins
Now the pasta is ready to serve :)

Chicken Alfredo 😋
Ingredients:
Olive oil
Chicken breasts
2 cups heavy cream
1 cup pasta water
1-1/2 c shredded Parmesan cheese
Spaghetti noodles
Seasonings- onion powder, garlic powder, Tony’s, paprika, Dan-o’s butter dust, oregano

Directions:
•add olive oil to a pan on medium heat
•once the pan is warmed up add the diced chicken breasts
•season the chicken with onion powder, garlic powder, Tony’s, paprika, Dan-o’s butter dust
•once the chicken is fully cooked add in heavy cream + pasta water and then season with garlic, onion, oregano and butter dust 
•stir to combine and add in Parmesan cheese
•mix and let the cheese melt
•once cheese is melted add in the noodles and give it a good mix 
~Now the pasta is ready to serve :)

En los años 80 México vivió una de las peores crisis económicas de su historia. Hubo momentos donde la inflación fue tan alta que los precios subían constantemente y el dinero perdía valor muy rápido.
En 1987 la inflación llegó a casi 160% anual, lo que provocó que muchas familias gastaran su sueldo inmediatamente porque guardar dinero significaba perder poder de compra.
Esta época de inflación extrema fue una de las razones por las que después México tuvo que quitarle tres ceros al peso.
Entender estas historias reales ayuda a comprender cómo funciona la economía y cómo proteger tu dinero.

Ingredients:  
- chicken (skinless and boneless thighs/drumsticks)
- Garlic and ginger paste (or 3 garlic cloves and a ginger thumb)
- 2tbsp green seasoning 
- 2 spring onions, diced
- 1 red bell pepper, sliced
- 1 green bell pepper, sliced
- 1 scotch bonnet 
- 1 red onion, diced 
- Fresh thyme 
- 2tbsp ketchup
- 2 chicken stock cubes 
- Drizzle of browning 
- 2tbsp brown sugar 
- Olive oil 
- 1tbsp jerk bbq sauce 

Seasonings: 
All purpose, smoked paprika, garlic granules, liquid maggi 

Method: 

1. Wash and dry your chicken. Remove and skin/bones if still on. 
2. Marinade the chicken with the seasonings, oil, a crumbled stock cube, browning, peppers, onions and thyme. The longer you leave it , the better it will taste.
3. Heat oil in a pan. Add brown sugar and let it caramelise until it's dark.
4. Add the chicken and cook until it's caramelised on each side then remove and set aside. 
5. In the same pan, fry the veg mix for 3 mins.
6. Return chicken to the pan. Add stock, thyme, scotch bonnet, ketchup and jerk BBQ sauce. 
7. Cover and simmer 45–60 mins.
8. Serve with rice and peas or white rice, plantain and slaw 🥰

If you’re trying to break into asset management, investment banking, or financial markets, these are some of the most common terms you’ll hear every day.

1️⃣ Yield
Yield is the return you earn on an investment, usually expressed as a percentage.
For bonds, it’s the income you receive relative to the price you paid.

Example:
If bond yields go up, bond prices usually go down.

2️⃣ Spread
A spread is the difference between two yields.
In credit markets, it’s often the difference between a corporate bond yield and a government bond yield.

Spreads help investors measure risk and relative value.

3️⃣ Long
Going long means you’re betting an asset will increase in value.
Example: buying a stock or bond because you believe the price will rise.

4️⃣ Short
Going short means you’re betting an asset will fall in value.
Investors borrow the asset, sell it, and aim to buy it back later at a lower price.

5️⃣ Liquidity
Liquidity refers to how easily you can buy or sell an asset without affecting the price.

Highly liquid markets = easier trading.
Low liquidity = wider spreads and more volatility.

If you want to work in asset management or the buy side, these terms will come up constantly in meetings, research, and interviews.

Top 5 Bloomberg Functions You Need to Know 📊

If you want to work in finance, trading, or asset management, these are Bloomberg functions you’ll see every single day.

1️⃣ TOP 
Your daily starting point.
Shows the top market headlines and breaking news — perfect for staying on top of what’s moving markets.

2️⃣ YAS 
One of the most used functions in fixed income.
Lets you quickly analyse a bond — yield, spread, duration, pricing — all in one place.

3️⃣ GP 
Turns any data point into a chart instantly.
Great for visualising trends, comparing data, and understanding market moves over time.

4️⃣ WEI 
World Equity Indices.
Gives you a snapshot of global equity markets — useful for quickly understanding how markets are performing.

5️⃣ SRCH 
Advanced search tool.
Helps you find bonds, companies, or securities based on specific filters — super useful for idea generation.

These functions alone can take you from confused on Bloomberg → actually useful in meetings.

Don’t get overwhelmed though — there are thousands of Bloomberg functions. You don’t need to know everything, just start with the basics and build from there.

It’s insane looking back at how bad it used to be. At this point it doesn’t even feel like I ever had achne. My whole teenage life I’ve struggled with achne which eventually led me to try Accutane. In addition to the 10X worse achne initially you also get really bad joint pain, severe dehydration, pretty bad nausea, and it really messes you up mentally. Ultimately it was the mental side effects that made me quit. At the time I was already struggling with severe bouts of depression and I had also started a new job. My medication window was always a half hour into my 8 hour shift and at that job I had to be very active and social with customers. After taking my Accutane I instantly couldn’t think of anything else but ending myself for the rest of the day so I quit it to keep my job. But now, 1 year later, just those two out of five months of Accutane have permanently restricted my body’s oil production to the point where recently I went for almost a full month without washing my face and didn’t get a single pimple. Would I recommend Accutane after my experience? If you are able to consistently cleanse and moisturize your face daily I would absolutely not. But if you think you can handle the SEVERE side effects and your as impatient as me then you might want to look into it.

Surviving Corporate Ep 2: Corporate stress isn't just burning you out. It's ageing your face.

Here's the biology 🧬:

Chronic stress breaks down collagen -> The protein keeping your skin firm and your under-eyes from looking like you just survived another Q4 close 😮‍💨

Why your under-eyes go first -> The skin there is the thinnest on your face. Add poor sleep, Thirsty Thursdays and team drinks into the mix and your body quietly stops prioritising skin repair. It switches into survival mode instead. And look, I'm not telling you to skip the drinks and I won’t be anytime soon. Corporate life is social and that matters. But knowing what's happening under the surface means you can work with your body, not against it 🍻

In a stressful corporate environment, your skin is fighting a daily battle. Here's what I personally do to slow the damage 🛡️

☕ Caffeinated Eye Cream Caffeine is a vasoconstrictor. It physically tightens blood vessels under the eye, reducing the pooling that causes dark circles and puffiness. Applied in the morning it firms the area and over time helps reduce chronic inflammation that accelerates skin ageing.

🌞 SPF Daily (No Exceptions) UV exposure breaks down collagen and elastin independently of anything else going on in your life. Your skin is already under pressure from a demanding job and broken sleep. SPF is the simplest thing you can add to your morning that directly slows visible ageing. No cream repairs ageing damage as well as preventing it.

⏰ No Caffeine After 2pm Caffeine has a half life of around 5 to 7 hours. A 3pm coffee is still 50% active in your system at 8 to 10pm. Poor sleep amplifies your stress response the next morning, which breaks down more collagen, which worsens under-eye ageing. Cutting caffeine early protects your overnight repair cycle, which is when most skin regeneration actually happens.

🚶 When stressed - Take a 5 Minute Walk During the Day. Even a short walk lowers stress, improves circulation and triggers endorphin release. Better circulation means more oxygen and nutrients reaching skin cells. Less stress means your body stays in repair mode longer throughout the day.

🫁 Double Inhale, Slow Exhale (If You Can't Leave Your Desk) Double inhale through the nose, slow exhale through the mouth. Repeat 5 times. Studies show this activates the parasympathetic nervous system within minutes, measurably reducing stress markers. When stress drops, your body switches back to repair and regeneration. Takes 60 seconds. Works.

🌙 Consider introducing a Retinol - it is a vitamin A derivative that directly stimulates collagen production at a cellular level, the exact collagen that chronic stress is breaking down. It also accelerates skin cell turnover, reducing the appearance of dark circles and fine lines over time. Start low (0.025 to 0.05%), use only at night, and always follow with SPF the next morning. One of the most clinically backed ingredients available in the world.

⚠️ Start once a week only. Your skin needs time to adjust to this active ingredient. Using it too often too soon will cause redness and irritation. Low percentage, low frequency, then build up slowly over weeks.

Save this for when your under eyes start doing more overtime than you do 😅

What Is Colocation In Trading?🏢

Colocation is when a firm’s trading servers are physically within the same data center as an exchange’s matching engine.

This proximity to the exchange greatly reduces network latency (time delay), which allows high-frequency traders (HFT) to receive market data and execute orders microseconds or nanoseconds faster than competitors, providing a critical competitive edge.

The Quirks of Natural Gas Futures!⛽️

Natural gas futures carry a well-known distortion around the March–April transition because it marks a hard shift from winter withdrawal season to spring injection season. March, the last winter contract, carries significant end-of-season storage risk, meaning prices can spike or collapse based on late-season cold or inventory tightness, while April reflects much softer, “shoulder-season” demand. This creates the infamous March–April spread—often called the widowmaker—where small weather forecast changes can produce outsized, nonlinear moves.

I wonder if I’ll ever feel like I have enough — and I say that as someone who has done a lot of things right with money.
the truth is, the feeling of “not enough” doesn’t go away just because the number gets bigger. I’ve been laid off. my partner was laid off this year. financial anxiety runs deep, and no savings account balance just erases that.

so if you’re doing the work and still feel scared — that’s not failure. that’s just being human.
part of the work is the mindset shift — learning to trust the progress you’re making even when it doesn’t feel like enough yet.

here’s what I keep coming back to though:
→ keep your emergency fund untouched (3–6 months of expenses)
→ build a second stream of income

You don’t need more motivation. You need fewer distractions and a system that makes focus easier.

1. Remove distractions before you even start:

Don’t rely on willpower mid-study. Put your phone in another room, log out of social media, and keep only the tabs you actually need. If distraction is not accessible, your brain won’t chase it.

2. Study in focused time blocks:
Instead of long, tiring sessions, use 45–50 minutes of deep focus followed by a 10-minute break. During that time, give full attention to one task only. No multitasking, no switching.

3. Define exactly what you’re going to do:
Saying “I’ll study chemistry” is too vague. Decide something like “revise polymers + solve 15 questions.” When your goal is clear, your brain stays engaged and less likely to wander.

4. Make your study space distraction proof:
Keep your desk clean and minimal. No unnecessary items, no noise, no visual clutter. A calm environment reduces mental chaos and helps you stay locked in longer.

5. Start small, but start immediately:
The hardest part is starting. Tell yourself you’ll study for just 5 minutes. Once you begin, resistance drops and focus builds naturally. Waiting for motivation only delays progress.

Distraction is not your personality. It’s just a habit you can rewire.

“I don’t know how to combine lifting and running”
Well… most don’t 🤷🏻‍♂️

Most who try to lift and run at the same time end up mediocre at both.

They either run so much they lose all their size and strength, or their lifts aren’t structured properly so they can barely jog a mile without their knees screaming or because of sore legs.

You do not have to choose between being strong and being fast. But you do need a system that builds both without one destroying the other.

This is how I structure a hybrid training week for my clients and for myself as someone who’s 220lbs lean, strong and fast:
✅ Monday - Upper Body Strength
✅ Tuesday - Speed or Tempo Run
✅ Wednesday - Lower Strength 
✅ Thursday - Easy Run (Zone 2)
✅ Friday - Upper Hypertrophy
✅ Saturday - Long Run
✅ Sunday - Full Rest

The key is intentional separation. 

Strength training is the priority in the gym with accessories for hypertrophy to get the “look”

Easy runs exist to build your aerobic base and burn more fat without trashing your recovery. 

Conditioning on lifting days build work capacity using Hyrox style movements like sled pushes, wall balls, and rower intervals so you are training for performance, not just aesthetics.

- 6 sessions. 
- No double days. 
- Fits a real schedule. 
- Builds a body that is strong, fast, lean, and built to perform.

Most people say they want to be great until they stand next to someone who actually is.

That’s where it gets real.

Because now it’s not motivation anymore. It’s comparison. It’s ego. It’s the uncomfortable truth that you’re not as far along as you thought.

And most people fold right there.

They convince themselves it’s not for them. They “stay in their lane.” They go back to what they’re already good at so they can protect how they feel.

But think about it…

If you only do what you’re already good at, you never become anything more.

The gap between you and someone elite isn’t a reason to quit. It’s the exact reason you should lean in harder.

That feeling of “I’ll never be that good” is the test.

Most people fail it.

The few who don’t are the ones willing to look at that gap and say, good. Now I know what’s possible.

So be honest with yourself…

When you see someone operating at a level you can’t comprehend yet, does it make you back off…

or does it make you step up?

They’ll always have something to say regardless…

They’ll judge you for staying the same.
They’ll judge you for trying to change.
They’ll judge you for getting started.
And they’ll even judge you when you win.

So if judgment is guaranteed…
why are you letting it stop you?

Most people hold back because they’re trying to avoid looking stupid.

But that’s the price you must pay to make it.

Every version of you that’s worth becoming comes with a phase where you look inexperienced, inconsistent, and unsure.

There’s no way around it.

The only difference is some people accept that part of the process and others use it as an excuse to never start.

At some point you have to decide:

Are you building your life…
or managing other people’s opinions?

#pursuepotential

Nobody prepares you for this part because all you ever thought about was making it pro.

Nobody talks about what happens after it’s over.

You go from structure, purpose, competition, identity…

to sitting at a desk wondering where that version of you went.

And if you’re not careful, you start convincing yourself that phase of your life is just… done.

That you’re “not that guy anymore.”
That you should just put all your energy into your career and making money.
That there’s nothing for you to train for anymore so “what’s the point?”

So you stop training like an athlete.
You stop pushing yourself.
You start settling into what’s comfortable.

Not because you can’t do more…
but because you forgot who you were.

Here’s the truth most people won’t say:

You didn’t lose it.
You just stopped demanding it from yourself.

The discipline, the edge, the standard, it’s still there.

But it doesn’t come back by accident.

You have to choose to bring it back.

So be honest…

Did you outgrow that version of you…
or did you just get comfortable without him?

I met Muko and her daughter Masani today.

Muko left Myanmar at 17, fleeing civil war. She built a new life here in Thailand. This is where she raised her daughter, and this is where she works. She weaves scarves by hand about 2 days for the smaller ones and up to 4 days for the larger pieces. Along with other hand man crafts. 

At first, I felt uncomfortable like I was at a zoo, staring at the latest captured animal. I know what it feels like to be seen as entertainment instead of a human being.

So I asked my guide first, then I asked her directly. She told me she welcomes it. Most people will never come here, and this is how they share their culture with the world.

Muko was wearing 27 rings. Masani was wearing 5. The rings don’t actually make the neck longer they slowly push the shoulders down over time, creating the illusion. Some say the tradition started as protection from tiger attacks. Others trace it back to their origin stories, tied to dragons and geese.

They usually begin wearing them around age five. Today, many daughters are given a choice. Most still choose to wear them, because they grow up seeing their mothers that way, and that becomes their standard of beauty.

- 2 large boneless, skinless chicken breasts (sliced horizontally into 4 thin cutlets)
Salt & freshly cracked black pepper
- ½ cup all-purpose flour (for dredging)
- 3–4 tbsp olive oil
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter (divided)
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- ½ cup dry white wine (like Pinot Grigio or Sauvignon Blanc)
- 1 cup chicken broth
- ⅓ cup fresh lemon juice
- ¼ cup capers
- 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
- Lemon slices (optional, for garnish)                                               Pat chicken dry.
Season both sides generously with salt and pepper.
Lightly dredge in flour, shaking off excess.
Heat olive oil and 1 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook chicken 3–4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through.Transfer to a plate and tent loosely with foil.
In the same pan, reduce heat to medium.Add garlic and sauté 30 seconds (don’t let it brown).
Pour in white wine, scraping up brown bits. Simmer 2–3 minutes.
Add chicken broth and lemon juice. Let simmer 5 minutes until slightly reduced.
Stir in capers.
Whisk in remaining 2 tbsp butter until sauce is glossy.
Return chicken to the pan and simmer 2–3 minutes, spooning sauce over top.
Sprinkle with fresh parsley and add lemon slices.

If you’re an Irish tax resident and investing in ETFs, this is what you need to know to stay on top of filing. 👇

Most EU-domiciled ETFs fall under Ireland’s fund rules.

That means:
• 38% exit tax
• An 8-year deemed disposal event
• Each purchase has its own 8-year clock

So here’s the simple system.

Open a spreadsheet.

Every time you buy, log the purchase.

Track:

ETF name
Platform
Purchase date
Units purchased
Price per unit
Total cost (including fees)
Deemed disposal date (purchase date + 8 years)
Market value at 8-year anniversary
Gain (value minus cost)
Exit tax due (38%)
Notes

That’s it.

One line per purchase.
One clock per purchase.

If you didn’t track from the beginning, don’t panic.
You can usually download your transaction history or account statements from your trading platform and rebuild this retroactively.

Tracking from day one turns panic into process.

Education only. Not personal financial advice.

Most people don’t think about this until it’s too late.

This is what we’re covering in Part 1 of my Irish Money Reality series on Building Wealth for Your Child. 

Part 2 covers the actual structures and options.

This is where people get tripped up.

It’s not the investing part - it’s everything around it.

Whose name it’s in.
When they actually get it.
And how it’s treated for tax.
	
Because in Ireland, you can build the exact same pot of money…

and end up in completely different positions depending on how you set it up.
	
In this video, I focused on structures that support investing.

Of course you always have the option to pay directly for large purchases (house deposit, etc) - tax efficient while keeping control. 

State Savings (DIRT-free) or simple savings in your child’s name are also options-  they just sit more on the ‘protect’ side than ‘grow’.

More complex Trust structures do exist, but those tend to sit in higher wealth / estate planning territory.

Education only. Not advice.

🧠 9 hobbies that genuinely sharpen your mind

1. 📚 Deep reading
Not summaries. Not threads.
Books that make you stay with ideas longer than is comfortable — and stretch your focus.

2. ✍️ Writing to clarify thinking
Not for posting.
Journals, notes, rough drafts.
Putting thoughts on paper so they become clearer.

3. 🛠️ Building a high-leverage skill
Coding, design, editing, writing.
Skills that compound over time instead of expiring.

4. 🚶 Walking without stimulation
No music. No podcasts. No phone.
Just your thoughts and your surroundings.

5. ♟️ Playing strategy-based games
Chess, logic puzzles, long-term strategy games.
Training foresight and decision-making.

6. 🧩 Studying human behavior
Psychology, observation, pattern recognition.
Learning why people act the way they do.

7. 🧘‍♂️ Intentional movement
Strength training or yoga.
Using the body to sharpen the mind.

8. 👀 Practicing visual awareness
Studying design, architecture, film, or art.
Learning to notice structure, balance, and detail.

9. 🎓 Teaching what you’re learning
Explaining ideas to others — or even to yourself.
Nothing tests understanding better.

✨ Intelligence isn’t built by consuming more.
📈 It’s built by practicing better habits consistently.

📚 How to Stay Active & Focused While Studying

1️⃣ Study at the Right Time ⏰
🌅 Early morning hits different (4:30–7 AM = fresh brain).
🍛 Avoid heavy study right after lunch.
🛏️ And please… don’t study on your bed (Bed = sleep mode ON).

2️⃣ Fix Your Sitting Setup 🪑
✔️ Use a chair & table.
✔️ Keep your back straight.
💡 Bright light is a must.
📖 Books at eye level = less strain, more focus.

3️⃣ Refresh Yourself 💧
❄️ Wash your face with cold water.
🚰 Keep a water bottle near you.
🥤 Sip water often.
🍋 Lemon water = instant refresh.

4️⃣ Be Smart with Drinks ☕
☕ Tea/coffee is okay (but don’t overdo it).
🚫 Avoid sugary drinks.
🌙 No caffeine at night — protect your sleep cycle.

5️⃣ Follow the 25–5 Rule ⏳ (Pomodoro)
📖 25 minutes deep study.
🧘 5 minutes break.
🚶 Walk, stretch, breathe.
🔁 Repeat.
This keeps mental fatigue away.

6️⃣ 2-Minute Energy Boost ⚡
🏃 20 jumping jacks.
🚶 Fast walking in your room.
🤸 Stretch neck & hands.
🌬️ 5 deep breaths.

➡️ Move your body = activate your brain.

7️⃣ Eat Light 🍎
🚫 Avoid heavy rice meals, oily food & overeating.
🥜 Choose fruits, nuts & light snacks.

8️⃣ Sleep Properly 😴
🛌 6–8 hours sleep is non-negotiable.
❌ Don’t pull all-nighters daily.
⏱️ If needed, take a 20-minute power nap (not 2 hours).

9️⃣ Make Study Active ✍️
❌ Don’t just read.
📝 Write notes.
👨‍🏫 Teach an imaginary student.
🧠 Solve questions.
🖍️ Highlight & speak out loud.

➡️ Active study = less sleepiness.

🚨 Emergency Tip (Very Sleepy?)

🧍 Stand and study.
🔊 Read loudly.
🔄 Switch subjects.
🔥 Start with the toughest topic first.

💪 Discipline > Motivation
Fix your habits, and focus will follow 💯

4. Rest is not quitting — I burned out thinking hustle was the only way. It almost cost me everything.
5. The version of you that started is not the version of you that succeeds — you have to be willing to change, again and again.

The Fear and Greed Index is a tool used by investors to measure the emotional sentiment of the stock market. It helps determine whether investors are acting out of fear or greed, two emotions that often drive market movements.

⸻

What the Extreme Fear vs. Extreme Greed Tool Is

The Fear and Greed Index ranges from 0 to 100 and reflects the overall mood of the market.
	•	0–24: Extreme Fear
	•	25–44: Fear
	•	45–55: Neutral
	•	56–75: Greed
	•	76–100: Extreme Greed

When the index moves toward 0, investors are very cautious and pessimistic.
When it moves toward 100, investors become overly confident and optimistic.

The concept behind the tool is simple: markets are driven by human psychology, not just fundamentals.

⸻

Extreme Fear

When the index shows Extreme Fear, it means investors are worried about losses. This often happens during:
	•	Market crashes
	•	Economic uncertainty
	•	Recession fears
	•	Major geopolitical events

During extreme fear:

📉 Investors sell stocks aggressively
💵 Money moves into safer assets like cash or bonds
📊 Stock prices often become undervalued

Many experienced investors believe extreme fear can create buying opportunities, because markets may be oversold.

A famous quote from Warren Buffett captures this idea:

“Be fearful when others are greedy and greedy when others are fearful.”

⸻

Extreme Greed

When the index shows Extreme Greed, investors are very optimistic and confident about the market.

This often happens during:
	•	Strong bull markets
	•	Rapid stock price increases
	•	High investor optimism
	•	Speculative bubbles

During extreme greed:

📈 Investors buy stocks aggressively
🚀 Risky assets become popular
💰 Valuations may become inflated

Extreme greed can sometimes signal that the market is overbought, meaning prices may be due for a correction.

⸻

What the Index Measures

The Fear and Greed Index uses seven different indicators to measure sentiment:
	1.	Stock Price Momentum – strength of market trends
	2.	Stock Price Strength – number of stocks hitting highs vs lows
	3.	Stock Price Breadth – overall participation in rallies
	4.	Put and Call Options – demand for protection vs speculation
	5.	Market Volatility – often measured by the CBOE Volatility Index
	6.	Safe Haven Demand – movement into bonds vs stocks
	7.	Junk Bond Demand – appetite for riskier debt

Together, these indicators provide a snapshot of market psychology.

⸻

How Investors Use It

Investors use the index as a contrarian indicator, meaning they often do the opposite of the crowd.

Examples:
	•	Extreme Fear → Possible buying opportunity
	•	Extreme Greed → Possible time to take profits

However, it should never be used alone. Professional investors combine it with:
	•	Fundamental analysis
	•	Economic data
	•	Technical indicators

⸻

Simple Example

Imagine the market drops sharply due to bad economic news.
	•	Investors panic
	•	Stocks sell off quickly
	•	The index falls to Extreme Fear

But if company fundamentals remain strong, long-term investors may see this as an opportunity to buy quality stocks at lower prices.

⸻

✅ In simple terms:
The Fear and Greed Index measures how emotional the market is, helping investors understand when markets might be overly pessimistic or overly optimistic.

In recent years, Amazon has periodically raised large amounts of capital by issuing corporate bonds to investors. A bond sale like this is essentially the company borrowing money from the public markets. Instead of taking out a traditional bank loan, Amazon sells bonds—debt securities that promise investors regular interest payments and repayment of the principal at a future date.

When Amazon conducts a bond sale, it typically works with major investment banks such as JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, and Morgan Stanley. These banks act as underwriters, helping structure the bonds, determine pricing, and sell them to institutional investors like pension funds, insurance companies, and mutual funds.

A typical Amazon bond offering is divided into multiple “tranches,” which are bonds with different maturities. For example, Amazon might issue bonds that mature in 3 years, 5 years, 10 years, or even 40 years. Each maturity has its own interest rate, known as the coupon. Shorter-term bonds usually offer lower yields, while longer-term bonds offer higher yields because investors are committing their money for a longer period of time.

Investors buy these bonds because Amazon is considered one of the safest corporate borrowers in the world. The company has a strong balance sheet, massive revenue from its e-commerce platform, cloud computing division Amazon Web Services, and diversified businesses including logistics, advertising, and streaming through Amazon Prime. Because of this financial strength, rating agencies such as Moody’s and S&P Global Ratings generally assign Amazon high credit ratings, which allows the company to borrow at relatively low interest rates.

One of the main reasons Amazon issues bonds—even though it generates tens of billions of dollars in cash flow—is financial flexibility. Bond financing allows the company to fund large strategic investments without immediately using its cash reserves. For instance, proceeds from bond sales may be used to expand data centers for AWS, build fulfillment warehouses, invest in artificial intelligence, acquire companies, or refinance existing debt at better rates.

Another reason is the current interest rate environment. If borrowing costs are relatively low, Amazon can lock in cheap long-term financing. This strategy became especially common after the monetary policies implemented by the Federal Reserve following the COVID-19 pandemic, which pushed interest rates lower and created strong demand for high-quality corporate bonds.

Demand for Amazon bonds is typically extremely strong. Large institutional investors view them as a stable investment that offers slightly higher yields than U.S. government debt issued by the U.S. Department of the Treasury. Because of this demand, Amazon’s bond offerings are often oversubscribed, meaning investors request more bonds than the company initially plans to issue.

From a broader market perspective, a major bond sale from a company as large as Amazon can signal confidence in credit markets and investor appetite for corporate debt. It also reflects how large technology companies increasingly use capital markets as a strategic financing tool rather than relying solely on equity or bank loans.

In summary, Amazon’s bond sales are large-scale borrowing events in which the company raises billions of dollars by issuing debt to investors. These offerings help finance long-term growth, maintain financial flexibility, and take advantage of favorable interest rates while providing investors with relatively safe, income-producing securities backed by one of the world’s most powerful companies.

A bond is essentially a loan made by an investor to a borrower. Instead of borrowing money from a bank, governments, municipalities, or companies borrow money from investors by issuing bonds.

When you buy a bond, you are lending money to the issuer for a specific period of time. In return, the issuer promises two things:
	1.	To pay regular interest payments, called the coupon.
	2.	To repay the original amount borrowed, called the principal or face value, when the bond reaches its maturity date.

For example, if a company issues a $1,000 bond with a 5% coupon rate and a 10-year maturity, the investor lends the company $1,000. The company then pays the investor 5% interest each year ($50). After 10 years, the company returns the original $1,000 along with the final interest payment.

Many bonds are issued by governments such as the U.S. Department of the Treasury, which sells Treasury bonds to help fund government spending. Corporations like Apple Inc. or Amazon also issue bonds to raise capital for investments, acquisitions, or expansion.

Bonds have several key features:

1. Face Value (Par Value)
The amount the issuer agrees to repay at maturity, often $1,000.

2. Coupon Rate
The fixed interest rate the bond pays to investors.

3. Maturity Date
The date when the bond issuer must repay the principal.

4. Yield
The actual return an investor earns if the bond is bought at a price different from its face value.

Bond prices can rise or fall in the market after they are issued. One major factor affecting bond prices is interest rates. When interest rates rise, existing bond prices usually fall because newer bonds offer higher yields. When rates fall, existing bonds become more valuable.

Investors often buy bonds because they are considered more stable than stocks and provide predictable income through interest payments. However, bonds still carry risks, such as interest rate risk, inflation risk, and credit risk if the issuer cannot repay the debt.

The February 2026 Consumer Price Index (CPI) report, released by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, showed that inflation in the United States remained relatively stable but still slightly above the target set by the Federal Reserve. Overall, the data suggested that price pressures in the economy are cooling compared with previous years, yet inflation has not fully returned to the central bank’s long-term goal of 2 percent.

According to the report, headline CPI increased 0.3% month-over-month in February, following a 0.2% rise in January. On a year-over-year basis, inflation remained at 2.4%, unchanged from the previous month. This indicates that while prices are still rising, the pace of inflation has stabilized rather than accelerating.  

The core CPI, which excludes volatile food and energy prices and is closely watched by policymakers, rose 0.2% for the month and 2.5% over the past year. This reading was largely in line with economists’ expectations and suggested that underlying inflation pressures are slowly moderating.  

Several categories played key roles in February’s inflation data. Shelter costs remained the largest contributor to overall inflation, though the rate of increase slowed. Housing prices rose roughly 0.2% during the month and about 3% annually, indicating that rent growth and housing inflation are gradually cooling compared with earlier periods.  

Food prices continued to rise moderately, increasing 0.4% during February, while energy prices rose about 0.6%, driven mainly by gasoline and utility gas costs. At the same time, some categories helped offset inflation. Used vehicle prices declined, new car prices were largely unchanged, and auto insurance costs fell slightly, providing downward pressure on the overall index.  

While the February report appeared relatively calm, economists caution that the data reflects conditions before a major surge in oil prices linked to geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Higher energy costs in March and beyond could push inflation higher in future reports if oil prices remain elevated.  

For financial markets, the report was interpreted as “steady but not fully cooled” inflation. Because inflation remains slightly above the Fed’s 2% target, policymakers are expected to remain cautious when considering interest-rate cuts. The data suggests the economy is moving toward price stability, but progress has slowed and inflation remains somewhat sticky.

In summary, the February CPI report showed stable inflation at 2.4%, modest monthly price growth, cooling housing inflation, and moderate increases in food and energy costs. While the report did not signal a resurgence of inflation, it confirmed that price pressures are still present and that the path back to the Federal Reserve’s target remains gradual.

I’m tired of two types of people.

The ones who, after any minor AI model update, scream “SWE IS SO OVER!!! YOU’RE DELUSIONAL IF YOU THINK OTHERWISE! THE END IS NEAR!!!” And the ones who always roll their eyes and proudly say “I never use AI” and shame anyone else who does.

Spoiler - they’re both wrong.

Don’t get me wrong, I use AI a lot on a daily basis, I like it, but I also see its advantages and disadvantages clearly.

Yeah, at some point AI will replace some programmers… the lazy ones. And it has nothing to do with AI’s capabilities. In today’s reality, you have to adapt, learn a lot, and master multiple things at the same time. If you can’t, if you don’t want to improve yourself, if you rely on AI only - REPLACED! Using Artificial Intelligence without Human Intelligence is a very bad idea 💀

And it’s equally stupid not to use it and deny how helpful it can be. Time is money, and AI can save you a lot of it. Denying such a powerful tool is just shooting yourself in the foot. I mean, if you already have a good technical knowledge, imagine how unstoppable you can be with AI by simply delegating a lot of things to it. Yeah, exactly.

So the point is: combine those two annoying types of people and find the balance. Use AI, but prompting alone won’t cut it - you still need good technical skills that allow you to understand what is going on and why.

Want to keep more of your hard-earned money this tax season? Here is a quick breakdown of how to reduce your tax bill in Canada.
➔ RRSP: Contributions directly lower your taxable income for the year. (The deadline is coming up on March 2nd!) 
➔ FHSA: Gives you an upfront tax deduction PLUS tax-free growth, as long as it's used for your first home. 
➔ Tax-Loss Harvesting: Sell investments that have lost value to offset the capital gains taxes you owe on your winning investments. 
➔ TFSA: Doesn't lower your taxes today, but all future investment growth and profits inside the account are 100% tax-free for life.

Bonus ways to save: 
➔ Tax Deductions: Don't forget to claim union dues, work-from-home expenses, moving costs, child care, and capital losses. 
➔ Charitable Donations: These provide tax credits, with a much higher credit rate applied to any donations over $200. 
➔ Self-Employed Write-Offs: If you have a business or side hustle, you can deduct legitimate expenses like internet, phone bills, and office supplies.

The Sony Rolly was one of the most playful pieces of tech from the late-2000s. Released by Sony around 2007, it wasn’t just a speaker—it was a tiny robot performer. The egg-shaped device would roll, spin, flap its side panels like arms, and flash colorful LEDs, all synchronized to the music it was playing.

You could load songs onto it or stream them via Bluetooth, and the Rolly would “dance” to the beat, turning a simple music session into a little light-show performance on your desk or floor. Sony even had software where people could program custom dance routines for different songs.

Looking back, the Rolly perfectly captured a time when tech companies experimented with fun, personality, and futuristic gadgets instead of minimal black rectangles. It felt like something straight out of a 2000s concept video—quirky, expressive, and a little ahead of its time.

In short: the Sony Rolly was less about perfect audio and more about joy—a dancing music companion from an era when gadgets tried to entertain you as much as they tried to impress you.
